title: Handshake thresholds and fidelity lanes SDK playbook
body:
Purpose and quick summary:
This doc proposes a practical set of SDK and API conventions to support latency-first streaming with graceful fidelity degradation and deterministic tool-call handshakes. The core idea is "fidelity lanes": runtime-negotiated quality/latency profiles combined with explicit handshake thresholds for tool invocation and structured output commitments.

Context and motivation (why this now):
- Customers add hosted streaming to low-latency UIs and mobile apps; they want predictable latency and clear downgrade semantics when model or infra capacity is constrained.
- Tool calls (webhooks, connectors, function calls) are brittle when partial output arrives or network flaps. We need deterministic commit points so SDKs can surface consistent UX.
- Current hosted streaming docs cover many streaming formats and progressive output patterns, but lack a small, opinionated surface for client SDKs to choose a latency/quality tradeoff and for servers to honor that preference while preserving safety and observability.

Goals (product outcomes):
- Provide SDK primitives that let developers pick latency-first or fidelity-first behavior with minimal code changes.
- Define a compact handshake protocol for tool invocation that is robust to partial streams and reconnects.
- Standardize a small structured-output checkpoint concept so clients can bind UI actions (render, call tool, save) deterministically.
- Produce telemetry/SLI definitions to measure fidelity transitions, tool call latency, tool success rate, and resumed sessions correctness.

Non-goals:
- Full streaming contract language (too heavyweight). Keep this an ergonomic playbook with 3–4 APIs to implement.
- Replacing every advanced SDK pattern in existing hosted SDK specs. This is a minimal surface for fastest adoption.

Key concepts (definitions):
- Fidelity lane: a declared preference with three named tiers (FAST, BALANCED, VERBOSE). Each lane maps to expected token-latency budgets and an optional quality target.
- Handshake threshold: a numeric value attached to a fidelity lane that determines when the server may (or must) defer tool invocation until a commit checkpoint is reached. E.g., threshold=0.6 means the server should delay tool call until incremental confidence >= 60%.
- Commit checkpoint: a short structured-output frame within the stream representing a stable intent and canonical arguments for tooling (JSON-ish text blob). Commit frames are idempotent and carry a resume token.
- Resume token: small opaque string clients use to resume or reconcile session state after reconnection. Not a full transcript; only commit-frames are required to be durable.

API sketch (server <-> client):
- Client opens a streaming request with: {model, fidelity_lane, handshake_threshold, resume_token?} (client SDK hides wire shape).
- Server begins token stream fragments. At key points, server may emit a "commit" frame: 
  ---COMMIT start---
  commit_id: <uuid>
  commit_type: "tool_call" | "render" | "checkpoint"
  body: <structured payload (stringified JSON)>
  resume_token: <short-token>
  ---COMMIT end---
- Only commit frames are guaranteed to be persisted for resumption. Regular token deltas are ephemeral.

Tool-calling handshake flow (recommended):
1) Client indicates fidelity lane and handshake threshold.
2) Server evaluates incremental signals; when commit criteria meet threshold, server emits commit frame with tool_call and canonical args.
3) The server may either: (A) perform the tool call on the server side and stream back the result as a commit of type "tool_result"; or (B) surface the commit frame and wait for client-side acknowledgement or instruction to execute.
4) If client disconnects before a commit, server will not run the tool unless a server-autonomous policy is configured (ops).

Example pragmatics (latency-first behavior):
- FAST lane: threshold defaults to 0.4, prefer server-side speculative tool calls when safe, emit short commits early. Ideal for chat UIs that want immediate autocompletions.
- BALANCED lane: threshold 0.7, server favors larger context before committing tool calls.
- VERBOSE lane: threshold 0.95, more conservative, prefer developer-visible confirmation.

SDK ergonomics (guidelines, intentionally simple):
- Surface two main client APIs: streamOpen(options) and onCommit(callback). Keep higher level: createSession instead of exposing low-level frames.
- Default options: {fidelityLane: "BALANCED", handshakeThreshold: 0.7, resume: true}.
- onCommit receives: {commitId, type, body, resumeToken}. Body is a string (stringified JSON); SDK may optionally try parse.
- Provide helper: executeTool(commit) which will either call the server-run tool or send an ACK to instruct server to proceed.
- Avoid forcing app authors to parse low-level tokens; commits are the main primitive they should care about.

Client code example (JS-like pseudo):
- const s = client.streamOpen({model: 'redwood-2-stream', fidelityLane: 'FAST'});
- s.onCommit(c => {
    if (c.type === 'tool_call') {
      // cheap UX: show placeholder, then confirm or call executeTool
      ui.showToolIntent(c.body);
      s.executeTool(c.commitId).catch(...);
    }
  });

Observability and telemetry (what to measure):
- % requests by fidelity lane.
- commit frequency per request (commits/request).
- average time from stream start to first commit for each lane (ms).
- tool-call arbitration ratio: fraction of tool_calls executed server-side vs client-ack.
- resume success rate: fraction of resume attempts that lead to a matching commit history.
- regression alerts: sudden spike in commit postponements or increase in tool-call failures.

Backward/compatibility considerations:
- If client doesn't send fidelity_lane, treat as BALANCED.
- For older SDKs that only consume raw token streams, still emit commit markers as textual frames (eg "---COMMIT") so they are visible but not required to be parsed.

Safety and security notes:
- Tool-call commit frames must include a server-side safety summary (short string) when server-side execution is speculatively allowed. This summary is surfaced to auditors and ops.
- Server should not execute side-effecting tools automatically for VERY_LOW trust models or unknown tenant configs. Default: explicit ack required for side-effecting ops in BALANCED/VERBOSE lanes.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (internal dogfood, 2 sprints): implement commit markers + resume token and integrate with hosted-api internal SDK. Metrics only.
- Phase 1 (beta clients, 4 weeks): expose fidelity lanes and the executeTool helper to SDKs. Invite 5 customers (low-risk).
- Phase 2 (gradual GA): enable server-side speculative execution for FAST lane with opt-in per-tenant config + strong telemetry and ops guardrails.

Open questions / TODOs (work backlog):
- How compact should resume tokens be to balance privacy and reconcilability? (security team input).
- Should we standardize an explicit schema for commit.body (e.g., typed tool contracts) or leave it freeform? Suggestion: initial freeform stringified JSON + later opt-in schema registry.
- Perf: commit frequency can affect throughput; SRE needs a simulation harness to model commit-heavy workloads.
- SDK UX: mobile SDKs may want to auto-ack small commits to reduce round-trip; what is safe default?
- Billing: when a server-side speculative tool call is executed and later rolled back due to model change, how is billing reported? (finance + product).

Appendix: quick checklist for engineers implementing the server side
- Emit commit frames with commit_id + resume_token.
- Persist commit frames to short-term durable store (30m?) to allow resume.
- Honor handshake_threshold in commit decision logic.
- Attach safety_summary for any speculative side-effecting tool call.
- Expose commit telemetry via console: commits/request, tool-call-latency, resume_success.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and conservative. Aim to keep server SDK surface small and move complexity to server-side heuristics and ops configs.
- Feedback wanted on threshold defaults, lane names, and the minimum set of commit fields.

Links / references: RDW-2148 (handshake prototype), internal meeting notes (slack #hosted-streaming), reference: previous drafts on progressive output and tool-handshake.
